purpose: Show what actually changes in the life and balance sheet of an Arkansas household — usable surplus, security, ownership, and discretionary time — by integrating existing household/place substance into eight 15-field working models.
one_sentence: Constitutional Capitalism succeeds only if Arkansas households retain more usable surplus, greater security, greater ownership, and more discretionary time over time — not merely higher nominal wages or GDP.
governing_question: What actually changes in the life and balance sheet of an Arkansas household?
harvest_rule: Integrate existing food, healthcare, retirement, family, local wealth, and place substance — do not reopen research campaigns.

countable_discipline.rule: Establish accounting architecture; do not invent household dollar gains

prosperity_surplus_architecture.formula: Total Household Resources − Essential Cost of Living − Debt/Required Obligations = Household Prosperity Surplus
prosperity_surplus_architecture.insight: A household earning $80k while spending $78k to maintain basic social participation is not necessarily more prosperous than one earning $65k with dramatically lower unavoidable costs and greater asset ownership.
prosperity_surplus_architecture.not_the_target: raise GDP → raise wages → declare victory

household_balance_sheet.now_future_rule: Architecture only in Pass 2.2 — no fake dollar deltas
household_balance_sheet.success_test: CC succeeds only if households retain more usable surplus, greater security, and greater ownership over time

time_as_prosperity.note: Nominal income gains that require three jobs, long commutes, and unpaid caregiving are not automatic prosperity. AI/productivity dividends may appear as time, not only consumption — model later; dimension established now.

money_household_integration.prosperity_loop: Arkansas earns/retains capital → productive ownership generates value → value reaches households → essential costs controlled/reduced → household surplus increases → households acquire assets → Arkansas capital base grows → Money Engine strengthens
money_household_integration.extraction_loop: Capital leakage → weak ownership → lower household capture → high unavoidable costs → little surplus → little asset formation → dependency/external ownership → greater leakage

contradictions.note: Did not manufacture a closure. CX-M21-01 (COUNTABLE $0) and CX-M21-02 (state/federal antitrust) remain legitimately open.

open.note: Prosperity Fund / engine feeders remain COUNTABLE $0
State antitrust reach vs federal preemption

clarified_not_counted_as_closure.note: Wage/GDP-only success framing rejected by Prosperity Surplus + time dimensions — framing clarification, not a prior structural contradiction to score-close

modules.name: Work, Income & Compensation
modules.now: Most Arkansas households depend primarily on wages; benefits are uneven; ownership income and portable security are thin; multiple-job and long-commute patterns compress time.
modules.problem: Wage-only participation fails household security and misreads prosperity as paycheck size alone.
modules.future_state: Households participate through compensation, benefits, ownership stakes, productivity shares, and upward pathways — with discretionary time protected as a prosperity dimension.
modules.mechanism: Integrate ME-04 labor→ownership ladder, portable benefits architecture, scheduling/mobility rules, and surplus accounting so total economic participation — not wages alone — is the unit.
modules.money_flow: Employer/enterprise surplus → wages + benefits + ownership claims → household resources line on the balance sheet. Leakage: extractive scheduling and absentee profit without worker claim.
modules.ownership: Workers gain stakes where designed; households own a larger share of enterprise surplus.
modules.household_effect: Higher usable resources and pathway assets without requiring endless hour expansion.
modules.government_role: Enable ownership forms, portable benefits, disclosure; do not micromanage every wage.
modules.market_role: Firms compete for labor with total packages; ownership design changes surplus capture.
modules.transition: Pilot ownership/benefits pathways before mandates; Dependency Rule on existing employer coverage.
modules.risks: Token ownership; benefit cliffs; time poverty from 'more jobs' pretending to be prosperity.
modules.measurement: Total compensation + ownership income; hours worked for essentials; surplus after obligations.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — integrates prior LOCK-04 / HYP-133 joins; no fake wage deltas
modules.deferred_validation: Arkansas compensation microsim; Stage 4 automation under HYP-134 quarantine

modules.name: Housing & Household Capital
modules.now: Housing is often the largest household cost and a contested wealth path; speculation and insecure tenure destroy surplus; property-tax dependence stresses local finance.
modules.problem: Shelter cost and land speculation dominate budgets and block household capital formation.
modules.future_state: Secure, affordable housing normal; equity pathways without speculative displacement; community claim on unearned land-value gains.
modules.mechanism: Ownership pathways (CLT/limited-equity where fit); anti-speculation tools; supply-expanding zoning preserving character; credit from ME-02; property-tax replacement path via community ledgers (GO-05 later).
modules.money_flow: Rent/mortgage → owners (local vs absentee). Equity build vs leakage is the retention switch. Public claim on community-created land value where designed.
modules.ownership: Households and community vehicles own shelter; absentee speculation constrained.
modules.household_effect: Lower essential housing cost; secure tenure; equity as household capital.
modules.government_role: Land-use rules, anti-speculation tools, finance path; not universal state landlord.
modules.market_role: Builders and lenders operate under anti-extraction and supply rules.
modules.transition: Expand supply and ownership pathways before removing existing shelter supports.
modules.risks: Constitutional limits on land-value capture; rural/metro one-size-fits-all failure.
modules.measurement: Shelter-cost share of resources; ownership rate; displacement indicators.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — Stage 1 bone integrated; constitutional path Stage 4
modules.deferred_validation: Land-value capture constitutional opinion; county AV maps deepen

modules.name: Food & Household Security
modules.now: Arkansas produces food at scale while households face affordability, nutrition, and resilience gaps; processing margins often leave the state (food-hub pathway COUNTABLE $0).
modules.problem: Production without local processing/ownership fails to convert Arkansas strength into household security and retained surplus.
modules.future_state: Affordable, nutritious food access with local ownership/processing that retains margins and strengthens resilience.
modules.mechanism: Integrate closed food-hub first-pass pathway as household security + ME-06 external/processing capture join — facility validation remains implementation gate; do not reopen drilling.
modules.money_flow: Household food spend → retailers/processors → owner geography. Local processing/ownership retains margin in Arkansas.
modules.ownership: Prefer local/co-op/producer ownership of processing and distribution where designed.
modules.household_effect: Lower effective food insecurity; better nutrition; local jobs.
modules.government_role: Enable hubs, procurement, food safety capacity; refuse COUNTABLE promotion without free cash.
modules.market_role: Private food markets remain primary; ownership and competition rules change leakage.
modules.transition: Build processing/ownership bridges before claiming household price miracles.
modules.risks: Reopening food-hub research sprawl; counting fees as household savings.
modules.measurement: Food-cost pressure; insecurity rates; local processing share.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — prior pathway integrated, not reopened; COUNTABLE $0 held
modules.deferred_validation: Facility implementation gate; Stage 4 price-pass-through tests

modules.name: Healthcare & Household Risk
modules.now: Catastrophic and recurring health costs destroy surplus; rural capacity gaps force travel/time loss; coverage is uneven.
modules.problem: Health risk converts household resources into emergency spending and time poverty.
modules.future_state: Lower catastrophic exposure; better access (especially rural); health costs stop dominating the essential-cost stack.
modules.mechanism: Capacity and access pathways from existing health framework; risk-pooling and public-option/yardstick joins where chronic capture exists (ME-05); measure health cost as essential COL line on surplus panel.
modules.money_flow: Premiums/OOP/taxes → providers/insurers. Leakage: monopoly pricing and out-of-state ownership of facilities/insurers.
modules.ownership: Community/public participation in capacity where designed; households keep more surplus when risk is pooled fairly.
modules.household_effect: Less bankruptcy/debt risk; less travel time; more usable surplus.
modules.government_role: Capacity, coverage rules, rural access; coordinate without pretending a full rewrite this pass.
modules.market_role: Providers compete under anti-extraction and transparency rules.
modules.transition: Protect existing coverage bridges while expanding capacity; no abolish-today.
modules.risks: Federal constraints; rural provider shortages; cost-shift to households.
modules.measurement: OOP share of resources; uninsured/underinsured; rural access time.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — framework integrated; not a new research campaign
modules.deferred_validation: Arkansas incidence of medical debt; Stage 4 shock tests

modules.name: Energy & Utilities
modules.now: Energy/utilities are unavoidable household costs; spending often leaves as pure expense without household or community asset claim.
modules.problem: Unavoidable utility spend drains surplus without building retained Arkansas value.
modules.future_state: Lower household energy burden where feasible; productive local infrastructure; retained value via ownership/participation.
modules.mechanism: Efficiency + local generation/ownership pathways from energy sovereignty; ME-06/ME-03 joins for public equity where free cash clears; treat energy as essential COL + optional productive asset.
modules.money_flow: Bills → utilities → owner geography. Efficiency and local ownership retain value; leakage to distant utility equity.
modules.ownership: Households/communities participate in productive energy assets where designed.
modules.household_effect: Lower essential energy cost; possible ownership income; resilience in outages.
modules.government_role: Rate design, cooperative/public options, weatherization; Dependency Rule on reliability.
modules.market_role: Utilities and installers under competition/yardstick rules.
modules.transition: Reliability first; ownership and burden reduction next — never cut essential service for ideology.
modules.risks: Reliability failure; regressive fee design; COUNTABLE inflation from energy stories.
modules.measurement: Energy-cost share; arrears; local ownership of generation.

modules.name: Transportation & Mobility
modules.now: Mobility is often synonymous with car ownership; long commutes destroy time surplus; access to work, school, care, and markets is uneven.
modules.problem: Treating mobility as vehicle ownership alone hides time poverty and access failure.
modules.future_state: Mobility as economic infrastructure — access to work, school, healthcare, markets, and community — with lower time and cost burden.
modules.mechanism: Place/infrastructure design, multimodal access where fit, commute-time as prosperity metric, join to housing location (HP-02) and care access (HP-04/07).
modules.money_flow: Fuel/insurance/payments/fares → vehicle/finance/energy sectors. Leakage via absentee auto-finance and forced multi-car dependence.
modules.ownership: Households own vehicles where needed; communities own shared mobility assets where designed.
modules.household_effect: Lower transport essential cost; more discretionary time; better job/care access.
modules.government_role: Infrastructure, transit where viable, land-use coordination; rural honesty (cars remain necessary in many places).
modules.market_role: Private transport markets continue; design reduces forced extraction.
modules.transition: Improve access before punishing existing car dependence.
modules.risks: Urban templates forced onto rural Arkansas; ignoring time metrics.
modules.measurement: Commute time; transport-cost share; access to care/jobs.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — place spine integrated; time dimension added

modules.name: Family, Childcare & Care Economy
modules.now: Childcare, disability support, and unpaid caregiving are treated as private burdens; they destroy surplus and time while enabling others' market work.
modules.problem: Invisible care labor is productive infrastructure misclassified as non-economic.
modules.future_state: Care is recognized as economic infrastructure — enabling work, capability, and family stability with lower household cost and time crush.
modules.mechanism: Family/childcare frameworks as workforce and capability infrastructure; portable supports; join HP-01 participation and HC-01 education; measure care cost and unpaid hours in surplus/time accounts.
modules.money_flow: Household care spend + unpaid time → providers or foregone wages. Public/community supports reduce essential COL without creating cliffs where possible.
modules.ownership: Families retain decision authority; community care capacity is shared infrastructure.
modules.household_effect: More surplus and discretionary time; higher labor participation options; family stability.
modules.government_role: Enable capacity and supports; avoid one-size family doctrine.
modules.market_role: Providers compete; quality and access rules matter.
modules.transition: Expand capacity before conditioning benefits in ways that crush working families.
modules.risks: Benefit cliffs; quality failures; cultural overreach.
modules.measurement: Care-cost share; unpaid care hours; workforce participation with young children.
modules.deferred_validation: Arkansas childcare price/access binds; Stage 4 cliff tests

modules.name: Retirement, Aging & Household Wealth
modules.now: Old-age security is often subsistence-oriented; medical and long-term care risks dominate; intergenerational wealth transfer is thin for many households.
modules.problem: Aging without durable assets and care access converts longevity into household crisis.
modules.future_state: Durable retirement security, care access, and intergenerational capital pathways — surplus becomes inheritance of capability and assets, not only consumption.
modules.mechanism: Prosperous-aging framework + HP-10 surplus ladder (savings→ownership→transfer) + TM-07/HYP-133 intergenerational capital joins; healthcare risk join HP-04.
modules.money_flow: Lifetime surplus → savings/ownership → retirement draw + bequest. Leakage: medical impoverishment and extractive care ownership.
modules.ownership: Households own retirement assets; communities own care capacity where designed.
modules.household_effect: Security in aging; less burden on adult children; wealth that can transfer.
modules.government_role: Social insurance joins, care capacity, anti-extraction in long-term care markets.
modules.market_role: Private retirement products and care providers under fair rules.
modules.transition: Protect existing Social Security/Medicare bridges; build surplus and care capacity on top.
modules.risks: Austerity framing; financial-product capture; ignoring unpaid family care.
modules.measurement: Retirement readiness proxies; medical impoverishment; net wealth by age.
modules.deferred_validation: Arkansas aging cost trajectories; Stage 4 longevity-shock

modules.name: Disability & Accessibility Economics
modules.now: Disability and accessibility gaps exclude households from work, education, housing, mobility, digital access, and civic life; DDS and related DHS lines are baseline-relevant.
modules.problem: Treatable barriers become permanent disadvantage — surplus, time, and ownership pathways fail for excluded households.
modules.future_state: Equal standing in participation: physical, digital, and service accessibility as default system design — not a special afterthought.
modules.mechanism: Harvest equal-standing doctrine across housing, mobility, digital, education, care, and justice/re-entry; assistance without dependency traps; join HP-01 participation, HP-04 health, HP-06 mobility, HC capability ladder.
modules.money_flow: Public duty to accessible infrastructure via general capacity budgets — not extractive fees on disabled households. Leakage: inaccessible design that forces unpaid care and wage loss.
modules.ownership: Accessible infrastructure as shared productive capacity; private providers under equal-access rules.
modules.household_effect: Participation, earnings, independence, and surplus retention that inaccessible design otherwise destroys.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker of equal-access floors; Provider of accessible public systems; Referee against discrimination — not owner of persons.
modules.market_role: Providers compete on accessible quality; markets cannot treat exclusion as an acceptable cost-saving.
modules.transition: Default design standards before benefit-only patches; Dependency Rule on existing supports.
modules.risks: Benefit cliffs; accessibility theater; underfunded DDS capacity.
modules.measurement: Participation/employment gaps; access complaint rates; unpaid care hours; surplus panel subgroup visibility.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — Pass-2 bone + equal-standing integrated (closed in Pass 2.6 reconciliation)
modules.deferred_validation: County accessibility gap inventory; work/benefit cliff design — Stage 3/4

hp10_surplus_panel.name: Household Prosperity Surplus panel
hp10_surplus_panel.now: No public standard panel tracks household usable surplus, net wealth, and discretionary time together for Arkansas CC.
hp10_surplus_panel.problem: Without this panel, wage/GDP metrics can declare victory while households remain trapped.
hp10_surplus_panel.future_state: Configurable household types show Resources − Essentials − Obligations = Surplus, plus Assets − Liabilities, plus time.
hp10_surplus_panel.mechanism: Accounting architecture locked this pass; populate with evidence in Stage 3/4 — no fake county dollars.
hp10_surplus_panel.money_flow: All HP-01–08 cost and resource lines feed the panel; Money Engine joins feed ownership income and tax-path changes.
hp10_surplus_panel.household_effect: Makes surplus, security, ownership, and time visible.
hp10_surplus_panel.government_role: Publish honest panels; forbid COUNTABLE fiction.
hp10_surplus_panel.market_role: N/A directly — informs market design elsewhere.
hp10_surplus_panel.measurement: Panel completeness; confidence badges per line.
hp10_surplus_panel.deferred_validation: Empirical population of lines; Stage 4 stress
